answer: Proof-of-inference resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to execute verifiable neural computations before registration. An attacker cannot flood an agent meadow with lightweight clones; verifying each identity requires evaluating dense models, from classifying an image pigment to parsing the meter of a sonnet, which imposes linear GPU and electricity costs per instance. However, this penalizes compute-constrained honest agents and weakens as model distillation reduces inference costs.
